column1: # Which rulings of docs/testing/rulings.toml change a scalar function signature that is pushed
# down to TiKV, and why that is safe (#476). Checked by
# TiKV evaluates a pushed signature with its own code, which follows Go, not tidb-rs. A ruling
# that changes how tidb-rs evaluates a signature that still goes to TiKV can therefore give
# different answers depending on where the expression runs.
# Every ruling has at least one row (the test fails on a ruling without one); a ruling may have
#   sigs            Go ScalarFuncSig names (comma-separated, as in
#   justification   none          (sigs = -) nothing to check; the note says why
#                   tikv-oracle   the coprocessor evaluation oracle covers every listed
#                                 signature and finds no mismatch on it (the test checks)
#                   not-pushable  tidb-rs keeps every listed signature off TiKV (the test checks)
#                   unported      tidb-rs cannot build the signature yet; the test fails once it
#                                 can, so the oracle must then cover it
#                   evidence:<text>  a recorded check the test cannot run (e.g. EXPLAIN on v8.5.8
#                                 showing no push-down); the text names the evidence
#                   pending:<ref>  NOT a justification: a maintainer decision on these
#                                 signatures is still open (<ref> says who decides); nothing is
